clause_evidence.reasoning: All 23 samples require learners to perform division as the primary mathematical operation. Samples span cloze, mcq, true_false, and error_detect formats, consistently testing the core competency of dividing one number by another to find a quotient or evaluate a division claim.

Samples adequately represent both remainder cases. Samples without remainder (e.g., 2000 ÷ 1000 = 2, 78 ÷ 6 = 13) demonstrate exact division. Samples with remainder (e.g., 51 ÷ 8 = 6 R 3 in sample 8dfa5824649def578f11, 60 ÷ 7 = 8 R 4 in sample e99e400248fdadbcee74) demonstrate division with a remaining amount. However, only two samples explicitly test the with-remainder case, giving lighter coverage to that sub-competency.

Eight samples test dividends in the 2- to 3-digit range: 78 (2-digit), 16 (2-digit), 158 (3-digit), 448 (3-digit), 75 (2-digit), 335 (3-digit), 12 (2-digit), 25 (2-digit). These represent the full specified range with both 2-digit and 3-digit examples, appropriate for the first competency category (2- to 3-digit by 1-digit without remainder).

Multiple samples divide 2- to 3-digit numbers by single-digit divisors with no remainder: 78 ÷ 6 = 13, 16 ÷ 8 = 2, 158 ÷ 2 = 79, 448 ÷ 7 = 64, 75 ÷ 5 = 15, 335 ÷ 5 = 67, 12 ÷ 4 = 3, 25 ÷ 5 = 5. All results are exact quotients with no remainder, satisfying this category.

Samples with 2-digit dividends in the with-remainder category are tested: sample 8dfa5824649def578f11 (51 ÷ 8 = 6 R 3) and sample e99e400248fdadbcee74 (60 ÷ 7 = 8 R 4). Both examples have 2-digit dividends and 1-digit divisors that produce remainders, aligning with the second competency category.

Two samples directly test division by 1-digit divisors that yield remainders: 51 ÷ 8 produces remainder 3, and 60 ÷ 7 produces remainder 4. Both require learners to find or evaluate a quotient-and-remainder pair, directly addressing the with-remainder division by 1-digit divisor requirement.

Dividends span the 2- to 4-digit range in the power-of-ten category: 70 (2-digit), 600 (3-digit), 2000, 6540, 5000, 3100, 6920, 8000, 4010, 8780, 3800 (all 4-digit). Samples cover the full specified range, testing division of 2-digit, 3-digit, and 4-digit numbers by powers of ten.

Samples test all three specified divisors. Division by 10 is tested in samples with dividends 6540, 6920, 70, 4010, 8780. Division by 100 is tested in samples with dividends 2600, 3100, 600, 3800. Division by 1000 is tested in samples with dividends 2000, 5000, 8000. All three power-of-ten divisors are represented, meeting the competency requirement.
